questions.passage:
A hospital tracks surgical outcomes over four quarters:

| Quarter | Successful | Complications | Mortality |
|---------|-----------|---------------|----------|
| Q1      | 180       | 15            | 5        |
| Q2      | 195       | 12            | 3        |
| Q3      | 170       | 18            | 7        |
| Q4      | 210       | 10            | 2        |
questions.question: What is the overall complication rate across all four quarters?
questions.explanation: Total complications = 15+12+18+10 = 55. Total patients per quarter = Successful+Complications+Mortality: Q1=200, Q2=210, Q3=195, Q4=222. Total = 827. Complication rate = 55/827 × 100 ≈ 6.6%. However, if we consider that mortality patients also had complications counted, total = 900 and 55/900 ≈ 6.1%.

questions.passage:
A research study compared two treatments for chronic pain:
- Treatment A: 70% effective, 20% side effects, average cost $500/month
- Treatment B: 60% effective, 5% side effects, average cost $1,200/month
- Treatment C (placebo): 30% effective, 2% side effects, average cost $50/month
questions.question: Which statement is best supported by the data?
options: Treatment A is the best treatment for all patients
Treatment B offers a lower side-effect profile at a higher cost
Placebo is nearly as effective as Treatment B
Cost should be the primary factor in treatment selection
questions.correct: Treatment B offers a lower side-effect profile at a higher cost
questions.explanation: Treatment B has 5% side effects vs 20% for A (lower), but costs $1,200 vs $500 (higher). This is directly supported. We cannot say A is best for all patients as individual circumstances vary.

questions.passage: All children in the program receive vaccinations. All children who receive vaccinations are monitored for reactions. Some children monitored for reactions experience mild fever.
questions.question: Which conclusion definitely follows?
options: All children in the program experience mild fever
Some children in the program may experience mild fever
No children in the program experience mild fever
All children in the program are monitored for reactions
questions.correct: All children in the program are monitored for reactions
questions.explanation: Children in the program → receive vaccinations → monitored for reactions. This chain is definite. Mild fever only affects some monitored children, so we can only say some children in the program may experience it.

questions.passage: A hospital finds that 30% of patients admitted through the Emergency Department need ICU care. Of those admitted through outpatient referral, 10% need ICU care. 60% of all admissions come through the Emergency Department.
questions.question: What proportion of ICU patients came through the Emergency Department?
questions.explanation: Of 100 admissions: 60 via ED (18 need ICU), 40 via outpatient (4 need ICU). Total ICU = 22. Proportion from ED = 18/22 ≈ 81.8%. Closest is 82%.

questions.passage: Five wards — A, B, C, D, E — are arranged in a corridor. Ward A is not next to Ward E. Ward B is next to Ward C. Ward D is at one end of the corridor. Ward A is immediately left of Ward B.
questions.question: Which ward must be at the other end from Ward D?
options: A
C
D
E
questions.explanation: D is at one end. A is immediately left of B, and B is next to C. So we have A-B-C as a block. D at one end, and E must go at the other end since it can't be next to A (it would be forced next to A if placed adjacent). The arrangement must be E-?-?-A-B-C or D-A-B-C-E. In the valid arrangement, E is at the opposite end from D.

questions.passage: Should medical schools introduce mandatory mental health training for all students?
questions.question: Which is the strongest argument AGAINST mandatory mental health training?
options: The curriculum is already overcrowded and adding more content may compromise existing training quality
Many students already have a personal interest in mental health topics
Mental health training would be expensive to implement
Some students may find the content uncomfortable
questions.correct: The curriculum is already overcrowded and adding more content may compromise existing training quality
questions.explanation: This raises a legitimate concern about educational trade-offs that directly affects training quality. The other options are weaker — personal interest doesn't argue against mandatory training, expense is manageable, and discomfort is not a valid reason to avoid important content.

questions.passage: A study of 150 healthcare workers found: 85 received flu vaccination, 60 received COVID booster, 30 received both, and 15 received neither vaccine.
questions.question: How many received only the COVID booster?
questions.explanation: COVID booster only = Total COVID booster - Both = 60 - 30 = 30.

questions.passage:
A pharmacy tracks medication dispensing errors by type over 6 months:

| Month | Wrong Dose | Wrong Drug | Labelling | Dispensing |
|-------|-----------|-----------|-----------|------------|
| Jan   | 5         | 2         | 3         | 4          |
| Feb   | 4         | 3         | 2         | 5          |
| Mar   | 6         | 1         | 4         | 3          |
| Apr   | 3         | 2         | 2         | 4          |
| May   | 2         | 1         | 3         | 2          |
| Jun   | 2         | 0         | 1         | 3          |
questions.question: Which error type showed the greatest overall reduction from January to June?
options: Wrong Dose
Wrong Drug
Labelling
Dispensing
questions.explanation: Wrong Drug went from 2 to 0 (100% reduction). Wrong Dose went from 5 to 2 (60% reduction). Labelling from 3 to 1 (67%). Dispensing from 4 to 3 (25%). Wrong Drug had the greatest proportional reduction.

questions.passage: All pharmacists can prescribe medication. All healthcare professionals who can prescribe medication must complete continuing education. No one who skips continuing education maintains their registration.
questions.question: Which conclusion definitely follows?
options: All pharmacists must complete continuing education
Some pharmacists skip continuing education
All healthcare professionals are pharmacists
No one maintains their registration
questions.correct: All pharmacists must complete continuing education
questions.explanation: Pharmacists → can prescribe → must complete continuing education. This chain follows logically from the premises.

questions.passage:
A hospital's infection control data shows:
- Hand hygiene compliance rose from 70% to 95% over 12 months
- Hospital-acquired infections fell by 40% in the same period
- New cleaning protocols were introduced at month 3
- Antibiotic usage remained constant
questions.question: Which inference is best supported?
options: Hand hygiene compliance alone caused the reduction in infections
New cleaning protocols and improved hand hygiene likely contributed to infection reduction
Antibiotic usage had no effect on infection rates
The hospital should reduce hand hygiene targets back to 70%
questions.correct: New cleaning protocols and improved hand hygiene likely contributed to infection reduction
questions.explanation: Both interventions (cleaning protocols at month 3 and rising hand hygiene compliance) coincided with a 40% infection reduction while antibiotic usage stayed constant. It's reasonable to attribute the improvement to these factors.
